text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Pakistan has started formal negotiations with the Taleban government in Afghanistan after a delegation led by its ambassador Aziz Khan arrived in the northern Afghan town of Mazar-i-Sharif on Monday.
- The National Assembly passed three bills on Monday that provide stringent laws for the recovery of bank loans.
- The Pakistan Railways may increase fares by five percent from July 1.
- About 4,500 Afghans studying in Pakistani madrassahs were sent to Afghanistan in the past few days to reinforce the Taleban frontlines in northern Afghanistan.
- A Pakistani national was executed in Saudi Arabia after he was convicted of smuggling heroin into the kingdom, a Saudi interior ministry statement said on Monday.
- The government is seriously contemplating the option of entering into a record $2 billion, three-year swap arrangement with private parties operating in the Gulf to avert the looming default.
- Spanish businessmen have shown interest in entering into joint ventures for marketing domestic appliances and communication equipment in Pakistan.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The International Monetary Fund and the Pakistani government have reached an understanding on the contours of Pakistan's budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), which is likely to have a huge deficit of around 125 billion rupees.

- The Pakistani government has proposed to the IMF to start a three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility for the country from fiscal 1997/98 with a target of reducing the budget deficit to five percent of the gross domestic product for the first year, which would be reduced gradually every year.

- President Farooq Leghari, while on a visit to the United Arab Emirates, called upon the business community there to explore opportunities of investment in Pakistan and urged them to participate in its privatisation process.
- The fate of the private power projects, now being discussed at various levels, will be decided by the Council of Common Interest at its meeting scheduled to be held in Islamabad on May 28.
- Foreign investment in Pakistan nose-dived to a meagre $633.7 million during the first three quarters (July-March) of fiscal 1996/97 from last year's total investment of $1,307 million.
NEWS
- The executive committee of the National Economic Council, in a meeting on Monday, approved a national drainage project of 31.4 billion rupees, which will be completed in 6-1/2 years.
- The government has suspended 18 officials of the Federal Investigation Agency on charges of corruption and misuse of authority.
MUSLIM
- Pakistan will convince the Central Asian republics to recognise the Taleban government in Afghanistan.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Monday that those found involved in fomenting sectarianism in the country would be hanged publicly.
--Islamabad newroom 274757
